title: Checkpoint directory names can inject HTML into the diff component
reasoning: Checkpoint discovery accepts arbitrary suffixes after the numeric component. Those directory names flow into name_a/name_b and are interpolated unescaped into HTML rendered by components.html. A crafted experiment directory can therefore inject markup and script event handlers into the diff iframe. This does not require a syntax-highlighting failure.
reproduction: Use a checkpoint directory named 'checkpoint_1_' containing a snapshot that differs from another checkpoint. Select it for comparison; the generated header contains an executable image element instead of literal directory-name text.
recommendation: HTML-escape both header labels before interpolation. Also escape raw source text in the syntax-highlighting exception path so every plain-text insertion remains safe.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No diff-viewer tests were included; escaping coverage for filesystem-derived labels cannot be verified.
suggestedRegressionTest: Exercise diff generation with HTML metacharacters and event-handler payloads in both labels, and with a highlighting failure; assert that untrusted text is escaped while intended highlighting markup remains intact.
minimumFixScope: Text escaping in generate_modern_diff and get_highlighted_line.
